# 2026-11-15 · NOC-329 · The Rust SDK's error messages are entries of texts.json, with placeholders, parts and one generated file per kind

- Decided by: coding agent, NOC-329 T2, within pm's decision on the format (texts/texts.json, a generator, committed generated files); pm, NOC-329, on the core's texts (slice T6) and on what stays a value
- Why: the Rust SDK builds 130 messages and pieces of messages. An error message is an entry of kind `error` named `error.<name>`, since many messages share one code; its `code` names the `ErrorCode` it is returned with, or several separated by ` | ` where the code depends on the failure (`storageFull | storageFailed`). A value goes into a text as a placeholder, `{name}` or `{name:?}` for its `Debug` form, and such a text generates a function that takes the values, so the wording stays in the file and only the values come from the code. A piece that goes into another message, such as a reason (`notAnInvitation`'s `why`), what failed, or the role a call needs, is an entry of kind `part`, without a code. The generated module is a folder, `crates/nocentraldb/src/texts/`, with one file per kind, so it stays under the repository's 700-line limit for a file. The gate finds a text written in code where `Error::new`, `Err` or a helper that builds an error (`invalid`, `failed`, `io`, `refused`, `holds`, `crypto`) is given a string literal, `format!` or `concat!`. The bridge's own messages, which the TypeScript SDK shows for a malformed request, move with the TypeScript SDK's texts in T3, so the gate skips `src/bridge/` until then. A message that passes on another component's text keeps that text as a value for now. The core's error texts that reach developers through the SDK (`viewFailed`, `lockRefused`, `notAPairingAnswer`, `recoveryCodeUnreadable`) fall under the owner's "every text developers see" too, and move in slice T6, in `ncdb-core`, last, after T5 (pm, NOC-329). A plugin's reason (`valueDoesNotFitBecause`) and the system's error (`ioFailed`) stay values: they are not the project's to word.
- Instead of: one entry per call, which would repeat each text shared by several calls; texts with positional `{}`, which would leave the order of the values to each call; or an allowlist of strings the gate does not read, which would let a new text in unseen.
- Topics: texts, sdk-rust, gates
